questions.question: Two runners on a 400 m track run at 5 m/s and 3 m/s in the same direction from the same point. They first meet after (seconds)
The same two runners (5 m/s and 3 m/s) run in opposite directions. They first meet after (seconds)
Two runners at 8 m/s and 12 m/s run in opposite directions on a 600 m track. They first meet after (seconds)
Two runners at 8 m/s and 12 m/s run in the same direction on a 600 m track. They first meet after (seconds)
A runner at 5 m/s takes how many seconds for one lap of a 400 m track?
A runner at 4 m/s runs 3 laps of a 200 m track in (seconds)
Two runners at 6 m/s and 8 m/s start together from the same point of a 400 m track and run in the same direction. They first meet at the starting point after (seconds)
questions.explanation: Both must complete whole laps: 6t and 8t multiples of 400 first at t = 200.

questions.question: Two runners with speeds in the ratio 3 : 2 run in opposite directions. The number of different points at which they meet is
Two runners with speeds in the ratio 5 : 3 run in the same direction. The number of different meeting points is
Two runners at 7 m/s and 9 m/s run in opposite directions on a 400 m track from the same point. The faster runner has covered at the first meeting (metres)
questions.explanation: They meet after 400 ÷ 16 = 25 s. The faster covers 9 × 25 = 225.

questions.question: Speeds 6 m/s and 4 m/s (opposite directions) give how many different meeting points on the track?
Two runners at 4 m/s and 6 m/s run in the same direction on a 600 m track from the same point. They next meet at the starting point after (seconds)
questions.explanation: 4t and 6t both multiples of 600: t = 300 s.

questions.question: A and B run on a 300 m track at 5 m/s and 3 m/s in opposite directions. After 90 s they have met (times)
questions.explanation: They meet every 300/8 = 37.5 s: at 37.5 s and 75 s, so 2 times by 90 s.

questions.question: A and B run in the same direction on a 400 m track at 8 m/s and 6 m/s. A has lapped B for the first time after (seconds)
Three runners at 4, 6 and 10 m/s run in the same direction on a 600 m track from the same point. All three are together again after (seconds)
questions.explanation: Pairs meet every 600/2 = 300 s and 600/4 = 150 s; all three after LCM(300, 150) = 300 s.

questions.question: Two runners at 3 m/s and 5 m/s run in opposite directions on a 160 m track from the same point. The number of times they meet in 60 seconds is
questions.explanation: They meet every 160/8 = 20 s, so at 20, 40 and 60 s: 3 times.

questions.question: Two runners at 4 m/s and 5 m/s run in opposite directions on a 360 m track from the same point. The distance of their first meeting point from the start along the first runner's path is (metres)
questions.explanation: They meet after 360 ÷ 9 = 40 s. The first runner has covered 160 m.

questions.question: Two runners start from the same point of a circular track and run in opposite directions at 6 m/s and 4 m/s. They meet for the first time at the start after (seconds). The track is 100 m.
questions.explanation: 6t and 4t must both be multiples of 100: t = 50 s.

questions.question: A track is 120 m. A runs at 3 m/s and B at 5 m/s in the same direction. A is given a head start of 20 m (B starts behind A). B catches up with A for the first time after (seconds)
questions.explanation: B gains 2 m/s on A, so it takes 20 ÷ 2 = 10 s to close the 20 m gap.

questions.question: Two runners on a 500 m track have speeds 5 m/s and 7 m/s, same direction. The number of times they meet in 15 minutes (900 s) is
questions.explanation: They meet every 500/2 = 250 s: at 250, 500 and 750 s, so 3 times.
